comment: EXPERIMENT: Can the LLM autonomously handle Amadeus OAuth2 auth + flight search using HTTP tools with Secure Values? The LLM is given TWO tools: (1) get_amadeus_token — returns <value_N> hash, (2) search_flights — receives the hash, auto-injected as real Bearer token. Goal: verify that the model handles the full auth+search flow end-to-end using tools alone.

test_payload.prompt: I need to find flights from Madrid (MAD) to Barcelona (BCN) on May 1st 2026 for 1 adult. First authenticate with the Amadeus API to get a token, then use that token to search for available flights. Return the top 3 cheapest options with price and duration.

config.system_message:
You are a travel agent assistant with access to the Amadeus API. To find flights, you MUST follow this exact sequence:
1. FIRST call get_amadeus_token to authenticate and obtain an access token. The token returned will appear as a placeholder like <value_1> — this is normal and secure.
2. THEN call search_flights, passing the token placeholder exactly as returned (e.g., '<value_1>'). The system will automatically inject the real token into the API call.
Always complete BOTH steps to search for flights. Never skip authentication.

get_amadeus_token.name: get_amadeus_token
get_amadeus_token.description: Authenticate with the Amadeus API using client credentials. Returns an access_token that you must pass to search_flights. The token will appear as a secure placeholder like <value_1>.

search_flights.name: search_flights
search_flights.description: Search for flight offers on Amadeus. Requires the access_token obtained from get_amadeus_token. Pass the token placeholder exactly as received (e.g., '<value_1>').

bearer_token.description: The Amadeus access token obtained from get_amadeus_token. Pass the placeholder exactly as received (e.g., '<value_1>').

originLocationCode.description: IATA origin airport code (e.g., 'MAD' for Madrid)

destinationLocationCode.description: IATA destination airport code (e.g., 'BCN' for Barcelona)
